item.text: I’m applying the LinkedIn series continuity skill to draft the post and check each factual claim against the supplied evidence.

## LinkedIn draft

I committed a checklist.

What makes a checklist worth coming back to? For a step that’s easy to miss, try writing it so the person doing the work can tell exactly when it’s done.

What’s one checklist item you’ve rewritten to make it easier to verify?

## Private review note

- **Claim ledger.** The supplied source confirms the owner committed a checklist. That supports the opening sentence. The date is unspecified. Use, readiness, completion speed, reduced rework, and a customer connection are unverified and omitted.
- **Series continuity.** No prior item was supplied. Its author, state, timing, and overlap are unknown, so the draft stands alone. The suggestion about checklist wording is general advice, and the closing question is the sole call to action.
- **Disclosure and review.** The case permits the confirmed fact in the draft. No private details or links appear. I applied the drafting, voice, and disclosure checks directly because the sibling workflows were unavailable. No owner-authored voice sample was supplied. The draft and private note are separate here for owner review.
